property_summary: In the correct contract, a Put call that would cause overflow reverts, preserving the invariant that balance <= previous balance + msg.value numerically; the buggy version allows overflow, resulting in a balance that is strictly less than msg.value when overflow occurs.

In the correct contract, after any sequence of Put calls, the contract's ether balance equals the sum of all individual msg.value amounts sent via Put (since overflow reverts); the buggy contract violates this by allowing an overflow in acc.balance, making the tracked balance inconsistent with actual received ether.

The reference contract guarantees that for any Put call, if it does not revert, the updated balance is strictly greater than the previous balance; the buggy version violates this by allowing overflow, making the new balance less than or equal to the previous balance.

After a non-reverting Put, the account's balance must be at least the msg.value sent; correct contract ensures this via overflow revert, buggy contract allows overflow wrap making balance < msg.value.

For any Put call that does not revert, the sum of balances across all accounts stored in Acc exactly equals the contract's ether balance (address(c).balance); the buggy version allows an overflow in Put, causing the stored balance to wrap and the sum of Acc balances to become inconsistent with the actual ether held by the contract.
After any call to Put, unlockTime must never be less than block.timestamp; the bug allows unlockTime to be set below block.timestamp.

After any call to Put, if _unlockTime is less than block.timestamp, the reference sets unlockTime to block.timestamp, while the bug sets it to the lower _unlockTime, making the unlock time less than the collection threshold block.timestamp right after the Put.

After a call to Put, the unlockTime in the buggy version can be set to an earlier point than the correct version ever would, effectively making funds immediately available for collection well before the actual block.timestamp.
After any Put, unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp at that point; the bug allows unlockTime to be lower, making acc.unlockTime < block.timestamp immediately.

After a call to Put, if a Collector contract subsequently calls Collect and fails to receive funds (triggering a revert), the reference C correctly deducts the balance while the buggy version allows a different unlockTime to have been set, but the crucial difference is that in the reference, a failed collect call leaves the balance unchanged while the buggy version's earlier unlock time could enable a collect attempt that succeeds earlier.

After any valid call to Put with a given _unlockTime parameter, the reference contract's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime is at least as large as max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp), whereas the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, so for any future _unlockTime, the reference Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime > block.timestamp while the mutant's equals block.timestamp.
After Put is called with _unlockTime > block.timestamp, the reference unlockTime must equal _unlockTime, while the buggy version sets it to block.timestamp instead.

After any Put call, if the provided _unlockTime is greater than the current block.timestamp, the reference contract's Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime must be at least that _unlockTime, while the mutant sets it strictly lower (to block.timestamp).

For any Put call with _unlockTime > block.timestamp, the reference contract's unlockTime must be >= _unlockTime, while the mutant sets it strictly lower to block.timestamp, making the reference satisfy the before-put condition that unlockTime >= _unlockTime but the mutant violates it.

After any call to Put, the reference contract's unlockTime equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp), whereas the buggy version always sets it to block.timestamp, so for _unlockTime in the future the reference asserts Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime >= _unlockTime but the mutant does not.
After any successful Put call, the caller's Acc balance must equal the sum of all previously deposited msg.value; the buggy version leaves the balance at zero.
For any caller, after a successful Put with any msg.value, the caller's Acc balance strictly increases by at least msg.value over any prior balance; the buggy version fails to increase it at all.

For any caller, after a successful Put, the caller's Acc balance recorded in the contract must be strictly greater than zero when msg.value is strictly greater than zero; the buggy version leaves the balance at zero.
After a Put with non-zero msg.value, the contract's total balance equals the sum of all account balances; the buggy contract holds ether that is not reflected in any user’s balance.

After a Put call with non-zero msg.value, any subsequent successful Collect call of amount _am by the same caller should succeed without reverting when _am <= msg.value; in the buggy version the balance is missing so the Collect call reverts.

In the reference, after any Put call, the unlockTime of the caller is >= block.timestamp of the Put transaction; the buggy version can leave unlockTime at its previous value, so after a call with a < block.timestamp _unlockTime later followed by an older _unlockTime, the final unlockTime may be < block.timestamp of the second call.

After calling Put with any _unlockTime, the caller's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp of that Put call; the buggy version omits the update, so a second Put with an _unlockTime < block.timestamp leaves the unlockTime unchanged, making it less than the second call's block.timestamp if the first _unlockTime was in the past.

For any actor and any two unlock times and values, after two Put calls, the caller's unlockTime is at least the block.timestamp of the second call in the reference, but the buggy version can leave it strictly less.

After any Put call, the caller's unlockTime is >= the block.timestamp when that Put was executed; the buggy version drops the update, so a second Put with a small _unlockTime leaves unlockTime unchanged and potentially < the second call's block.timestamp if a prior Put had set it to a past value.

After any two consecutive Put calls by the same actor, where the second call has a non-zero msg.value, the caller's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp of the second call; the buggy version drops the unlockTime update, so the unlockTime can remain equal to the block.timestamp of the first call, making it less than the second call's block.timestamp.
After a call to Put, the contract's balance equals the sum of all Acc[user].balance entries; the bug doubles the msg.value addition, breaking this invariant.

After any sequence of calls to Put and Collect, the contract's balance is at least the sum of all holders' balances; the bug doubles msg.value in Put, making the contract balance exceed the sum of holders' balances.

After any call to Put, the contract's balance equals the sum of msg.value plus any pre-existing balance; the bug double-adds msg.value, making the contract balance exceed the sum of msg.value plus the previous balance.
After a Put call, the balance of msg.sender must be equal to the previous balance plus the msg.value sent; the bug adds msg.value twice, making the balance equal to previous balance plus 2*msg.value.

LogFile's public History array length must strictly increase only when Put succeeds (no overflow revert), but the mutant increments it even on revert, breaking the invariant that History length growth implies successful state update.
LogFile.History length must never increase if Put's require fails (e.g. on overflow) — the mutant adds a message before the require, so a failing Put still adds to History.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the sum of all msg.value arguments in Acc[msg.sender].balance must equal the total value actually held by the contract for that sender; the mutant logs AddMessage before the overflow check, causing a revert that still emits a log but does not update the balance, breaking the invariant that AddMessage call implies balance update.

For any Put call, if the call reverts due to the balance overflow require, then no new Log message must be recorded in History; the mutant adds the message before the require, so a reverting Put still increases History length.
Collecting any amount reduces the sender's balance by at most the collected amount plus any dust from integer rounding, but M subtracts one extra unit.
